*   The Brightloom checkout API experienced a 43-minute SEV-1 outage on 14 March, resulting in HTTP 503 errors for 100% of payment-confirmation requests, affecting approximately 18,400 customers and causing an estimated 2,150 abandoned orders.
*   The root cause was a configuration error where a merge conflict resolution dropped the `env: staging` guard, causing a staging-specific reduction of `max_client_conn` from 2000 to 200 to be applied to the production environment.
*   The incident was resolved by reverting the configuration at 09:55 UTC, with the error rate returning to baseline by 10:02 UTC after engineer Sam Okafor identified the incorrect value in the production config.
*   Action items include adding a CI check to reject pooler changes without explicit environment keys, alerting on connection pool saturation above 80%, and processing refunds for affected orders estimated at 6,300 EUR.
*   Positive aspects of the response included updating the status page within 6 minutes of the initial alert and completing the configuration rollback in under 3 minutes.

*   Tidewater CLI 4.2.0, released on 2 October, requires Node 18 or newer and drops support for Node 16.
*   Key features include parallel uploads (up to 8 files, default concurrency 4), resumable transfers via `tidewater push --resume`, and a new `tidewater doctor` command for system checks.
*   Breaking changes involve the removal of the `--legacy-auth` flag (requiring `tidewater login`) and a change in `tidewater list` default output to JSON when stdout is not a terminal.
*   Fixes address a Windows crash with trailing dots in paths, an incorrect exit code for remote checksum mismatches, and misleading `--dry-run` help text regarding session file writes.
*   Housekeeping updates include moving documentation to docs.example.com, updating the Homebrew formula, basing the Docker image on Alpine 3.19, and acknowledging 14 community contributors.

*   Mobile onboarding completion rose to 61% from 48%, though a 30% drop-off persists at the notifications permission screen, prompting a plan to move the prompt after the first saved item.
*   The notification prompt change will ship in Android version 3.7.2 and iOS version 3.8 (planned for 3 December) due to the iOS build freeze on 19 November.
*   The pricing page A/B test showed Variant B (annual-first layout) converting at 4.1% versus 3.4% for the control, leading to a decision to roll out B with a 10% holdback for two weeks.
*   The office move is scheduled for 15 January, and the support backlog discussion is deferred to the following Thursday.

*   The draft RFC-0042 proposes an optional `Idempotency-Key` header for API v3 to prevent duplicate orders, addressing 312 support tickets (0.4% of orders) from last quarter.
*   The server stores keys with request body hashes and responses in Redis for 24 hours, returning stored responses for matching keys, `422` for body mismatches, and `409` for in-flight requests.
*   Storage utilizes the existing Redis cluster with a `idem:` prefix, estimated at under 2 KB per record and 40 GB at peak load, while PostgreSQL was rejected due to write latency.
*   Alternatives such as automatic key derivation and mandatory headers were rejected to prevent merging legitimate identical orders and to maintain backwards compatibility, respectively.
*   Open questions remain regarding configurable TTLs per customer and whether to extend coverage to `PATCH` requests, with the author leaning against the latter.

*   The system aims to reduce sprint usage from the current 78% to a target of 30–40% by implementing stamina costs and a "winded" state that reduces speed to 60% for 3 seconds when stamina reaches zero.
*   Stamina mechanics include a maximum of 100 at level 1 (increasing by 5 per level up to 150), a drain rate of 12 per second while sprinting, and regeneration of 8 per second after a 1.5-second delay.
*   Sprinting is disabled when carrying heavy objects or in water deeper than knee height, and a full sprint from 100 stamina lasts approximately 8.3 seconds, covering about 62 meters at 7.5 m/s.
*   Dodge rolls cost a flat 20 stamina and remain available during the winded state, while cooking buffs like "Hearty Stew" provide +20 maximum stamina for 10 minutes and mounted travel ignores stamina entirely.
*   Open issues include determining if the winded state requires a unique animation (currently reusing the idle-breathing loop) and implementing a separate heavy-breathing audio cue tracked under ticket AUD-211.

*   The customer’s month-end reporting was blocked because CSV exports for their 410,000-record workspace failed at 50% due to a 15-minute worker timeout.
*   A temporary workaround raising the timeout to 40 minutes allowed the customer to successfully complete the export in 27 minutes, unblocking their reporting deadline.
*   The customer received a 10 EUR account credit as an apology while the permanent streaming fix is scheduled for release on 6 Feb.

*   Q3 revenue reached 18.6M USD, representing an 11% increase from Q2 and a 24% year-on-year growth, with subscription revenue accounting for 15.9M USD.
*   The company ended the quarter with 1,284 paying accounts (a net gain of 73), reduced gross churn to 2.3%, and increased enterprise accounts to 47.
*   Gross margin improved to 74% due to an 8% reduction in cloud hosting costs, while operating margin improved to -6% from -9% in Q2.
*   Q4 qualified pipeline stands at 31M USD with a 22% forecast win rate, and headcount increased to 412 employees, including 11 new engineering hires.
*   Key risks include two enterprise renewals worth 2.1M USD ARR facing budget freezes and potential billing confusion from new pricing tiers launching on 1 December.

*   A 21-day pilot study of 96 university students found that daily text-message reminders to wind down 45 minutes before bedtime reduced mean psychomotor vigilance task lapses by 1.8 compared to a control group, while increasing self-reported time in bed by 22 minutes.
*   The study had limitations including a convenience sample of psychology students, the absence of a placebo message for the control group, and a short duration that did not test effects beyond 21 days or during high-stress exam periods.
*   The authors concluded that reminders may modestly improve morning attention and noted that a larger preregistered trial is planned for spring.

*   Effective 1 January, Managed Plus monthly fees increase by 6.5%, though customers signing a 24-month renewal before 15 December retain current pricing until 30 June.
*   Service levels improve with uptime raised to 99.95% and service credit caps increased from 30% to 50% of the monthly fee.
*   Backup retention extends to 35 days, with an optional add-on available for longer retention at 0.02 EUR per GB per month.
*   The termination notice period without cause extends from 60 to 90 days, while the 30-day cure period for material breach remains unchanged.
*   Phone support shifts to weekdays 07:00-21:00 CET, and Meridian Backup GmbH is added as a sub-processor for off-site backups.

*   New hires receive a pre-shipped laptop and meet their buddy at 10:00 on Day 1, with a manager joining at 14:00 for goal setting, while waiting for IT to enable accounts before installing work tools.
*   Access to GitHub, the cloud console, and on-call tools is granted within 48 hours, but production access requires completing a 90-minute security training, and a VPN client is mandatory for remote work.
*   During Week 1, new hires must read the architecture overview in the `platform-handbook` repository, merge a "first PR" by Friday, and attend the Wednesday engineering demo at 16:00.
*   In Week 2, new hires shadow an on-call shift with their buddy (without carrying the pager alone until week six) and select a starter ticket labelled `good-first-issue` from the board.
*   Practical details include monthly lunch vouchers, Tuesday kitchen restocking, a parking lot closure for resurfacing until month-end, and support via the #new-hires channel and Thursday People team office hours.

*   The lamp-keeper boss in level 2 lacks a visible telegraph for its second phase, causing an unfair difficulty spike that led three testers to quit.
*   The jump buffer is too short for gamepad users, and the dash button is not currently remappable.
*   The camera clips through walls in narrow corridors, and two testers experienced mild motion sickness during the rooftop chase.
*   Frame rate drops to approximately 40 FPS on a GTX 1050 in the market scene, and one unreproduced crash occurred when loading level 3.

*   The company is moving from Levent to Maslak on September 30, with the old office closing on September 27 at 18:00 and remote work required between September 27 and 30.
*   The new office opens on October 2, but only 120 desks will be available for the first week, necessitating a rotational work schedule for teams.
*   Personal items must fit into two company-provided boxes by September 25, while monitors and laptops are handled by IT; unlabeled boxes will not be moved.
*   Parking is limited to 40 spots with applications due by September 18, the company shuttle continues from Levent at 08:15, and the new office is within walking distance of the metro.
*   The cafeteria on the 2nd floor will serve only lunch for the first two weeks, coffee machines are not yet installed, and employee cards remain valid in the new building.
